transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood), Martin Kline (CISO, Fairview), Aisha Rahman (Head Cloud Ops), Leo Torres (SWE), Dana Holt (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro - Jordan Reyes, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya our SE.
[00:12] Martin: Hey Jordan, hi Priya. Thanks, Martin here, CISO at Fairview. We'll mostly be looking at security posture for hosting models that will touch PII.
[00:22] Priya: Great, Martin. Can you tell us what you're evaluating — hosted, dedicated or private? And any must-have controls?
[00:30] Martin: We're trying to understand where Redwood fits. Our preference is hosted for dev teams but for production with PII we might need private or at least dedicated with bring-your-own-keys. Must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs to Splunk, KMS/HSM control, and clear data retention/erasure.
[00:52] Aisha: Also network constraints: we need VPC peering or private link, and we want to know about egress paths for logs.
[01:05] Jordan: Totally. At a high level Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For hosted we have SOC2, and we can offer customer-managed KMS for certain contracts; for private you get full control and the control plane can be customer-managed.
[01:25] Leo: Quick question - for dedicated, how do you handle key management? Do you support CMEK?
[01:30] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated we can support CMEK patterns and integrate with customer KMS solutions. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our keys by default, and we can offer BYOK in enterprise contracts — that gives you the HSM control you need.
[01:45] Martin: What's the difference in audit logs between Hosted and Private? Can we forward every request/response metadata to our SIEM?
[01:54] Priya: We emit rich audit logs including request id, model version, route, latency, and user id metadata. For Hosted we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding (syslog/S3 sink) and have audit export; for Private it's under your control so logs live in your environment and you can ship them however you like.
[02:12] Martin: Any redaction concerns — we don't want full responses in logs if they contain PII.
[02:18] Priya: We support configurable logging levels — metadata-only by default for PII-sensitive flows. You can opt-in to include full payloads, but we recommend metadata + pointers to encrypted payload storage.
[02:30] Dana: From procurement: what compliance evidence can you provide upfront? We need SOC 2 report, ISO, and a vendor security questionnaire.
[02:38] Jordan: We'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 certificate, and a completed standard vendor questionnaire. I'll include contact for our security team for any follow-ups.
[02:48] Aisha: Network: do you support VPC peering or private link into your hosted infra? How do you handle NAT/egress for model downloads?
[02:58] Priya: For Hosted we have VPC peering or PrivateLink options for enterprise connections — it's part of the Private/Dedicated offering. For model hosting we use pull-based deployments over secured channels; egress is via a managed NAT gateway but for Private you'd control NAT. Note: sometimes transcript says peer ring or VPC peer ring in logs, but we mean VPC peering.
[03:22] Leo: About RBAC — can we map our SAML groups to Redwood roles and limit which teams can call which models?
[03:28] Priya: Yes. We support SSO/SAML SAML 2.0 and SCIM user provisioning. You can map groups -> roles, and define per-route/model permissions in the Console. There are default roles and fine-grained RBAC for models, routes, and billing.
[03:45] Martin: Encryption — at rest, in transit, and key ownership. Do you use customer keys in Hosted?
[03:52] Jordan: In Hosted default keys are Redwood-managed, but we offer BYOK/CMEK for enterprise contracts; Dedicated can be configured to use customer KMS. In Private deployment you control keys entirely. All traffic is TLS-encrypted in transit.
[04:08] Aisha: For certifications, how recently was SOC2 performed and can we get the auditor contact?
[04:14] Jordan: SOC 2 Type II is current through 2026-11; we'll send the report and the auditor POC in the package.
[04:22] Martin: Data residency — our regulators require all PII for EU customers to stay in EU regions. How do you handle region pinning?
[04:29] Priya: We support region pinning and routing by policy. For Hosted we can route requests to EU regions and ensure model artifacts and logs are kept in-region under particular plans; for Private you deploy in your chosen region.
[04:45] Leo: Any limitations on model size / custom model uploads in Private vs Hosted?
[04:50] Priya: Private supports larger model artifacts and can be tuned for GPU memory / quantization; Hosted has curated model catalog with verifed performance profiles, and larger bespoke models are recommended for Private/Dedicated.
[05:05] Martin: Retention & deletion — we need the ability to request deletion of historical logs and model query traces. SLA for deletion?
[05:12] Priya: We have defined retention policies and can support data deletion requests. For Hosted we can purge customer data on request; for Private it's controlled by you. We'll outline the deletion SLA in the docs we send.
[05:25] Dana: Procurement note — pricing model differences for Dedicated vs Private? We'll expect a different contracting path.
[05:31] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit; Private is a platform licensing model. We'll include high-level pricing and contract flow in the follow-up.
[05:40] Martin: Any known gaps in compliance that we should be aware of? Third-party pen test cadence?
[05:46] Jordan: We run annual third-party penetration tests and rolling internal scans. We'll include the pentest summary and remediation timelines.
[05:56] Aisha: Do you support forwarding to our Splunk instance for audit streams?
[06:02] Priya: Yes — we support syslog/S3 sinks + direct SIEM integrations; we'll include a sample config for Splunk.
[06:12] Martin: Can we get a hands-on benchmark? We want to run a short latency/cost test with representative prompts and PII redaction in place.
[06:20] Priya: Absolutely — we'll schedule a technical deep-dive. For that we'll need a small dataset, access patterns, sequence lengths, and acceptable SLOs.
[06:30] Jordan: Recap next steps: Jordan will send SOC2/ISO and vendor docs; Priya will send network checklist, Splunk config, and schedule deep dive; Martin will share compliance reviewer list. Any other blockers?
[06:45] Martin: No blockers, timeline is: compliance review in 2 weeks, technical benchmark the following week.
[06:53] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2) and "VPC peer ring" transcription glitch for "VPC peering"; "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash".
